newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian troops turn back some 50,000 refugees.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian troops turn back some 50,000 refugees.

text.p: Troops and police set up a roadblock in northwest Tanzania on Friday, turning back up to 50,000 Rwandan refugees leaving their camps, a U.N. World Food Programme official said.
The official said Tanzanian troops and police established the roadblock about four km (2.5 miles) southeast of Lumasi camp, cutting off the tail end of a stream of refugees leaving since Thursday.
"There was some chaos while the refugees decided what to do but there were no signs of shots being fired or resistance," the U.N. official said. "The refugees just turned around and headed north."
"Clearly the majority had already passed and it was a last ditch attempt but they stopped the last 40,000 to 50,000, who headed back towards the Benaco (region) camps," the official added.
U.N. officials earlier said up to nearly half a million Rwandan and Burundian refugees were leaving or had already left their camps and were trekking away from Tanzania's border on Friday.
Before the exodus from the Tanzanian camps started last Sunday, Lumasi had a population of some 113,000 refugees.
Sadako Ogata, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, appealed to Tanzanian authorities on Thursday to redirect the refugees back towards their camps without using force.
